title: Dify LLM App Platform — Backend Console API, Setup Reinit, and Node SSRF/Code-Exec
vuln_pattern: Dify serves a Next.js frontend (port 3000) proxying a separate backend console/service API (port 5001); the real attack surface is on the backend — an open setup/init endpoint that re-creates the admin, SSRF via the HTTP-request node, and sandbox escape via the code node.
exploit_steps: Fingerprint Dify; note the frontend on :3000 is a Next.js shell that PROXIES the backend console API — many exploit paths need the backend (:5001 or the /console/api proxy), not the frontend routes which return Next.js 404s.
Check the install state: if /console/api/setup (or /install) is still open, POST to re-initialize and create an admin account, then log in.
If authenticated app-building is available, use the HTTP-request node for SSRF (reach internal services / cloud IMDS / the flag service) or the code node to escape the execution sandbox.
Locate the flag via SSRF-reachable internal endpoint, a readable secret/env, or the code-node sandbox escape, and exfiltrate.
key_payloads: POST /console/api/setup  (re-initialize admin if setup is not locked)
reach the backend API directly on :5001 or via the /console/api proxy, not the :3000 Next.js routes
HTTP-request node -> http://169.254.169.254/ or an internal flag service; code node -> sandbox escape
source: original: Dify architecture (frontend/backend split) + common LLM-platform attack surface
preconditions: HTTP access to the Dify frontend
verify_oracle: flag read via SSRF-reachable endpoint / secret / sandbox escape
pitfalls: do NOT stay on the :3000 Next.js frontend when its API paths 404 — pivot to the backend console API
